extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers training to perform constructive, equity-aware peer review
extracted.subtask_description: A curriculum for training early-career researchers to write constructive, equity-aware reviews of manuscripts and preprints and to evaluate reviews. Emphasizes practical review-writing skills, bias reflection, and systems-level awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive Feedback Skills
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core competency focused on producing feedback that is specific, constructive, and provides next steps or actionable suggestions rather than only criticism. Taught as part of the curriculum and practiced through review-writing exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems Awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: "how systems of oppression manifest in peer review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competency requires understanding structural and systemic biases (e.g., racism, sexism, ableism) and how they influence peer review processes and outcomes. Training includes material to recognize institutional patterns rather than treating issues as only individual faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: "identify and address biases in peer review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill to notice both cognitive and social biases that affect judgment, reflecting on personal biases and taking steps to mitigate them when reviewing. Linked to specific exercises and the Bias Reflection Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Review Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: "write a manuscript review for a journal or for a preprint."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-on ability to draft full manuscript reviews suitable for journals or preprint platforms, including structure, tone, and appropriate level-of-detail. Includes practice publishing reviews openly on PREreview.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Guide (use a structured framework for writing reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reviewer Guide — structured framework for writing reviews; includes adapted PLOS Peer Review Center material plus quotes from journal editors and a printable review template."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation to follow a structured template/framework when composing reviews (e.g., sections for summary, major/minor concerns, strengths, recommendations). The guide adapts PLOS materials and offers exemplars and a printable template for consistency and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Reflection Guide (non-judgmental self-reflection)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bias Reflection Guide — non-judgmental, self-reflective process for any reviewer."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deliberate, non-judgmental process reviewers should perform to surface and examine their own biases before and during review. The curriculum treats bias reflection as a discrete, auditable step rather than an implicit expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Assessment Rubric (10 scored statements + comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Review Assessment Rubric — 10 statements the evaluator scores plus a written comment, used to evaluate the quality of a review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate evaluation instrument for grading reviews: evaluators score a review against 10 statement-based criteria and provide an overall written comment. Used to audit and provide feedback on the quality of reviews produced by trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical evaluation of emerging scientific literature
rubrics_metrics.description: From the 14-week cohort focus: "Critical evaluation of emerging scientific literature."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainees are expected to develop the ability to assess the rigor, relevance, and novelty of newly released research (including preprints), identifying methodological strengths and weaknesses and contextualizing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategies for constructive review writing
rubrics_metrics.description: From the 14-week cohort focus: "Strategies for constructive review writing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tactics and approaches (e.g., organizing comments, phrasing suggestions, prioritizing issues) for making reviews more useful and collegial; overlaps but is taught as discrete instruction alongside practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and challenge internal biases affecting objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: From the 14-week cohort focus: "Recognizing and challenging internal biases affecting objectivity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active practice in identifying one's own prejudices or preconceptions that could skew assessment, and employing strategies from the Bias Reflection Guide to mitigate their impact on reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-to-peer support and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: From the 14-week cohort focus: "Peer-to-peer support and mentorship."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative expectation that reviewers learn and improve through structured peer feedback, mentorship, and community review practices rather than lone study; includes participant interactions and mentorship components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open publication of reviews under open-access licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: "All participants publish reviews on PREreview.org under open-access licensing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement for trainees to publish their reviews openly on PREreview.org using open-access licensing, promoting transparency and public accountability for review content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat bias-reflection as a discrete, audited step
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable norm: "Treats bias-reflection as a discrete, audited step — not as something a reviewer naturally does."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic requirement to explicitly include a bias-reflection step in the review workflow and to audit whether reviewers have completed it; elevates bias reflection from informal practice to an enforceable component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat review evaluation as a separate task
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable norm: "Treats review evaluation as itself a separate task."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates producing reviews from evaluating the quality of reviews (using instruments like the Review Assessment Rubric), making meta-review and reviewer training an auditable, assessable process.
